parole.testo: From a Turkic language. First attested from the early 13th century. Compare Ottoman Turkish طابور (tabur).

From a Turkic language. Compare Chuvash чӗр (čĕr), Crimean Tatar tiz, Turkish diz (“knee”).
Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries).

parole.significato: law (a binding regulation or custom established in a community)
parole.testo: Unknown origin. The -vény ending seems to be a noun-forming suffix, however, it cannot be proven due to the unclear etymon. parole.significato: bustard (any of several large terrestrial birds of the family Otididae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Chuvash-type Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Cognates include Kyrgyz тоодак (toodak).

parole.significato: trap, snare (a device designed to catch animals)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Common Turkic *tor. Compare Kazakh тор (tor), Azerbaijani tor.

parole.significato: to endure, tolerate, bear, put up with, brook
parole.testo: From a Turkic language, most likely Oghur (compare to Old Chuvash *tör-, tür-), from Proto-Turkic *töŕ- (“to bear, endure, suffer”). Probably a word loaned during the Magyars’ presumed part in the Onogur tribal alliance.

parole.significato: to crumple, roll, roll up, tuck in (e.g. the bottom edge of a shirt under the belt of trousers)
parole.testo: From a Turkic language. Compare Turkish dürmek.

parole.significato: trough (a long, narrow container, open on top, for feeding or watering animals)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from a Chuvash-type Turkic language. Compare Tatar ulaq, Crimean Tatar oluq. First attested in 1121.

parole.significato: false, fake, sham, phoney, make-believe, bogus, pseudo-, counterfeit
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries).

Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), from Proto-Turkic *arpa. The sense “bacterial infection of the eye” is perhaps a calque of scientific Latin hordeolum (“stye”), from Latin hordeolus.

parole.significato: gantry (a supporting framework for a barrel)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). First attested in 1480.

parole.significato: To reach or extend until a point.
parole.testo: Uncertain; perhaps from a Turkic language, compare Uyghur [script needed] (er-), Chagatai [script needed] (ir-), Turkish er- (“to reach”) verb forms. The second main meaning derives from the first, ér (“to reach”).

parole.significato: merit, worthiness (a deed worthy of respect and appreciation)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). (cf. Turkish erdem).

parole.testo: First attested in 1372. From a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *es. Compare Chuvash ас (as).

parole.significato: to write (optionally to someone: -nak/-nek, about someone/something: -ról/-ről)
parole.testo: From a Turkic language; compare Chuvash ҫыр (śyr), Turkish yazmak (“to write”).

From Turkic *aɣïl; compare Chuvash ял (jal). Borrowed before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *āɣïl.

parole.significato: buzzard (various hawks and other birds of prey in the subfamily Buteoninae)
parole.testo: Via a Turkic language (compare Yakut элиэ (elie), itself a borrowing from a Mongolic language) from Old Mongolian, compare Mongolian элээ (elee).

parole.significato: Armenian (of or relating to Armenia, its people or language)
parole.testo: From a Turkic language. Compare Ottoman Turkish ارمنی (ermeni, “Armenian”).

parole.significato: heifer (young female cattle, i.e. young cow)

parole.significato: suslik, ground squirrel ('Spermophillus citellus', a small burrowing furry rodent)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries).

parole.significato: to guard, herd, watch, keep safe
parole.testo: Uncertain. Either from a Chuvash-type Turkic language or derived from őr.
